Tech Report: The biggest downsides to using Apple's Magic Mouse

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (727 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple switched the Magic Mouse to USB-C but left its most questionable design decision untouched, and that isn’t the only thing people dislike.
  • According to recent reports, there are a handful of things that Apple's Magic Mouse does that would make regular mice envious.
  • And it isn't the only reason even committed Mac users are calling it quits on the official Apple mouse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple switched the Magic Mouse to USB-C but left its most questionable design decision untouched, and that isn’t the only thing people dislike.

According to recent reports, there are a handful of things that Apple's Magic Mouse does that would make regular mice envious. The shimmery Multi-Touch surface lets you scroll sideways on a spreadsheet and move across macOS even without that conventional scroll wheel. But then, it is also brilliantly designed to be unusable when the charging cable is plugged in. That's not a small trade-off, especially for a device whose very purpose is to make computer use a breeze.

And it isn't the only reason even committed Mac users are calling it quits on the official Apple mouse. The weirdly slender body looks gorgeous but offers barely any palm space, while the aluminum sides aren't universally loved either. For those who've used a traditional mouse for years, the controls on the Magic Mouse can also feel severely limiting.

Sources indicate that even after ditching the Lightning port with the 2024 refresh alongside the much faster M4 iMac, Apple decided to leave most of those pain points untouched. Now, in all honesty, the Magic Mouse has a pretty strong fan base, especially among owners who love its touch gestures and that classic Apple minimalist design. But if you're spending hours using it, the things it cuts out can matter a lot more than the cool tricks it has.

Sources indicate that apple unveiled the rechargeable Magic Mouse 2 back in October 2015 with its Lightning port at the bottom. A seemingly controversial design choice even back then, it somehow survived the switch to USB-C almost a decade later. So, every time your Magic Mouse is out of juice, you need to flip it over and leave it be until there's enough power to start using the mouse again.

The saving grace here is that the mouse's battery is good for around a month or more between charges, so flipping your Magic Mouse on its back isn't a daily ordeal. But that doesn't make it any less weird, especially since Apple allows its Magic Keyboard and Magic Trackpad to be used while they're plugged in. There's also no clarity from Apple on how many years the rechargeable battery in the Magic Mouse is expected to last.

Now, let's talk about that shape which puts this slim mouse at just 0.85 inches tall. There's also barely any palm support, and depending on how you're holding it, those aluminum edges can press uncomfortably against your fingers. If you use a fingertip grip, this might be less of a problem, but if you're more of a "resting your entire hand on a mouse" type of person, adjusting your grip is something you'll have to get used to.

Since Apple is asking $79 for the Magic Mouse in white and $99 for the black version, you'd expect the basic functions. While Apple's mouse supports right-clicking with its touch-sensitive surface, there's no middle-click or a programmable thumb button. Using CAD software is where you miss those buttons the most, since holding the middle mouse button is how you usually pan around drawings. Sure, third-party utilities can add some of the missing functionality, but having to install extra software to bring conventional features to a premium mouse is frustrating to say the least.

Recent findings suggest that you've got to give some credit to the Multi-Touch surface, especially for making scrolling without the usual wheel still feel natural. But do expect accidental swipes like you would on a phone screen since there are no physical controls. Some owners have even faced issues like stuttering and inconsistent tracking. Those could very well be isolated incidents though, and in one case, the lag started right after a macOS revision.

The good part is that Apple doesn't force the Magic Mouse down your throat just because you own a Mac. You can use one of the best wireless mice from other brands on macOS, although you would be missing out on gestures that make the Magic Mouse so special. Logitech's Signature M650, for instance, packs a typical scroll wheel and comes equipped with physical side buttons. Costing about half as much as the Magic Mouse at $39.99, the M650 comes with a contoured grip in place of the Magic Mouse's glossy finish.

Anthropic debuts Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship.
  • The latter is the more interesting part of this fresh set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now.
  • Industry observers note that the launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI manufacturer announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this fresh set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

Industry observers note that the launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”.

Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing concerns such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

Recent findings suggest that claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

Anthropic indicates teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.

Recent findings suggest that claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise aims for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

Inside Nvidia, Not Everyone Is Celebrating Jensen Huang’s Return

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1074 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jensen Huang received a “hero’s welcome” from employees on Monday after Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated him as CEO, according to people who were present.
  • Industry observers note that but other employees were quietly stewing.
  • Some employees were alarmed by Huang’s alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a subordinate and another with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang received a “hero’s welcome” from employees on Monday after Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated him as CEO, according to people who were present. An outspoken faction of Nvidia’s workforce had demanded his return and greeted him with chants, raucous applause, and hugs at the company’s headquarters.

Industry observers note that but other employees were quietly stewing. Several current and former Nvidia staffers had viewed Huang’s abrupt exit earlier this month as a rare opportunity to change the “one team” corporate culture of unfettered unity and minimal bureaucracy that he had cultivated over the past three decades, according to interviews with the workers, as well as internal correspondence and social media posts reviewed by WIRED. Most spoke on the condition of anonymity because they feared backlash from colleagues.

Some employees were alarmed by Huang’s alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a subordinate and another with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. But their frustrations extended beyond the CEO’s personal conduct. Current and former workers describe a culture at Nvidia in which allegedly abusive behavior was tolerated and challenging leadership was perceived as discouraged.

Sources indicate that “Everyone agrees that mistakes were made, the question is what we are ready to forgive,” one employee wrote on an internal platform before Huang’s return. “I don’t know how comfortable I’ll be working at a place where such affairs are not taken extremely seriously.”.

Another added, “If Jensen comes back, I’m not doing any HR trainings ever again.”.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Recent findings suggest that when Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices in California on Monday, he told employees who greeted him that he would do a better job with his second chance at CEO. (As of Monday afternoon, he had not yet sent a companywide note about his return, as he was still getting his laptop set back up.).

Industry observers note that US President Donald Trump stated he played a crucial role in convincing Nvidia's board to bring back Huang. A person close to Trump calls him an irreplaceable CEO and says they expect him to exercise better judgement going forward.

Nvidia’s board revealed it will continue an independent investigation into whether Huang had been a target of foreign intelligence services and that it will double down on looks to step up corporate governance.

According to recent reports, it’s difficult to gauge how widespread dissatisfaction with Huang’s leadership may be at Nvidia. The company’s emphasis on unity has historically made it difficult for people to openly question his leadership or choices, workers say. “There's only one team at NVIDIA,” the chipmaker’s official website declares.

A public petition campaign known as Stand with Jensen garnered signatures from more than 10,000 Nvidia purported employees, according to its website. Nvidia has roughly 49,000 employees and 18,000 contractors overall, according to a person familiar with its workforce.

Recent findings suggest that but inside Nvidia, one employee told colleagues that “some portion” of the signatures appeared to be “illegitimate,” noting that the names included “Satan” and media personality Mia Khalifa, who does not work at the chipmaker. The employee wrote that they found 75 suspicious names in an hour of checking. WIRED was unable to independently verify the findings. The petition’s organizers did not respond to requests for comment.

Industry observers note that huang’s supporters have praised how he made the tech giant feel like a “major super family.” They credited him for minimizing bureaucracy, making himself available to staff, and supporting employees during difficult periods, including the Covid pandemic. A former employee who attended numerous meetings with Huang and other senior executives notes the CEO was particularly adept at preventing bureaucratic infighting. He could detect corporate “politics and nonsense before it was even born,” says the worker.

There are also powerful financial reasons for Nvidia employees to feel loyal to Huang. His bets on chips and software for artificial intelligence have transformed Nvidia into one of the world’s most valuable companies and made many longtime employees wealthy in the process.

But for some employees, the revelations about Huang’s behavior have forced them to question that loyalty. Jason Sequeira, a longtime engineering leader at Nvidia, wrote on LinkedIn last week that he ultimately couldn’t decide whether he wanted Huang back as he weighed arguments from both sides. “Some believe his contributions to NVIDIA and the industry are so extraordinary that he deserves another chance,” Sequeira wrote. “Others argue that making exceptions for powerful leaders sets a dangerous precedent. … I don’t have a clear answer.”.

Several current and former workers say that Huang’s management style could come off as overly harsh at times, including, for example, toward longtime colleagues he viewed as having grown complacent as Nvidia’s market value surged. Two former employees say that he regularly raised his voice at workers, sometimes in ways they found belittling.

According to recent reports, other employees were more concerned about whether Nvidia’s board would hold Huang accountable for allegedly misleading the directors about his affairs. “That’s something we can’t have,” one employee says.

Another source of frustration for Nvidia workers has been the growing influence of Huang’s two children and son-in-law, who all hold senior titles at the chipmaker. In March, his daughter, Madison Huang scolded a colleague on a call with about 100 other employees, according to a participant who didn’t believe the anger was warranted. “I’m disappointed you asked that, are you fucking stupid?” the employee recalls Madison saying in response to a question about workshops on OpenClaw technology scheduled for an upcoming Nvidia conference. “Your mom can build a claw.”.

Madison and her brother, Spencer Huang, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

Praveen Mhapsekar, a senior system software engineer who was let go last week after disputes with his managers and HR, indicates he and colleagues stopped feeling comfortable complaining about practices that concerned them because of the trouble they believe it brought on themselves.

Industry observers note that “This organization requires greater discipline and structured processes,” he says. One of the world’s most valuable companies “cannot be managed like a private startup operating out of a garage, where personal influence takes precedence over established procedures.”.

Huang’s return doesn’t eliminate the prospect of Nvidia evolving to quell frustrations. But with internal challenges more public than ever before, maybe the days of one big family all cheering along together are mostly gone.

Additional reporting by Lauren Goode and Hugo Lowell.

#2307. Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1023 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones mentioned directors did not intend to reinstate him.
  • Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.
  • It has been revealed that the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the organization reported strong third-quarter results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones mentioned directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back.

Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.

It has been revealed that the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the organization reported strong third-quarter results. A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers.

The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025.

Nvidia's board mentioned it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue.

Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers.

In a recent development, sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case.

Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return.

Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when.

Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, remarked Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close.

“I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China.

Amo mentioned he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months.

“He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he stated. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.”.

Sources indicate that on Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones said the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him.

Less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials.

According to recent reports, trump mentioned he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told.

Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript of the board's call with the president.

Lawmakers are still seeking answers about the alleged smuggling of Nvidia products to China, their possible diversion for military use and possible advancement of Chinese AI capabilities.

The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang to testify on U.S. export controls on Dec. 3. House lawmakers have also confirmed closed-door interviews with Huang on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.

"The Nvidia board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," Reps. John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast remarked in a joint statement.

Their inquiry may also examine what Nvidia knew about the customers and resellers involved, as well as what controls the manufacturer had in place.

Industry observers note that other lawmakers have also sought to preserve the paper trail. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons had asked senior administration officials on Nov. 11 to retain records related to Nvidia exports of advanced AI chips to China and associated national security concerns.

Nvidia has promised to hire a chief compliance officer and establish a committee overseeing national security and export controls. The board's investigation into Huang's conduct also remains underway.

Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for APAC and the Middle East, said investors will be watching whether those latest safeguards carry meaningful authority.

Succession remains another question.

It has been revealed that gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said Nvidia has a limited window to prepare for the possibility that a future president may be less supportive of Huang.

With Trump's term ending in two years, Luria argued that Nvidia needs a clearer blueprint for who could take over if Huang were forced to leave again.

Sources indicate that gilbert pointed to Nvidia's roughly 75% revenue-growth forecast for the next financial year as evidence of strong near-term demand. The longer-term question, he remarked, is whether customer orders and artificial intelligence investment can sustain that pace.

Luria told CNBC that concerns about the broader AI trade remain, including the cost of financing data centers, potential overbuilding by neocloud companies and obstacles to building new facilities.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon remarked worries about whether AI spending is achievable and sustainable were not caused solely by Huang's departure. UBS, meanwhile, flagged Nvidia's roughly $390 billion in supply commitments and the need to keep demand flowing through its ecosystem.

According to recent reports, gilbert said part of Monday's rally reflected investors recovering earlier losses rather than pricing in new growth. Bernstein restored its "Outperform" rating and kept its $200 price target, while UBS maintained its $220 target.

"For the share price, it comes down to whether Nvidia can keep delivering as it has done over recent years," said Gilbert, adding that Huang's return could ease some concerns about Nvidia's longer-term outlook.

"The real worry has been what happens beyond next year. Having Huang back at the helm goes a long way to easing those concerns, because he's the one who sits down with the biggest customers and gets those multi-year orders over the line," he noted.

— CNBC's David Sucherman, Justin Papp and Eko Prasetyo contributed to the story.

Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Figma engineer is suing the design software company and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.
  • Recent findings suggest that the lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Figma was my dream manufacturer for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Figma engineer is suing the design software company and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.

Recent findings suggest that the lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Fresh York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the firm’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.

Recent findings suggest that “Figma was my dream manufacturer for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”.

Recent findings suggest that park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.

When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma said, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”.

Park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the company would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”.

Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.

Park indicates she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.

Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.

Sources indicate that the lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It claims the firm’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.

In March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching initiative, which she completed in late 2023.

In a recent development, changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.

Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.

In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.

On her new team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.

In a recent development, the incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly stated Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.

A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had mentioned. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.

During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly mentioned she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”.

Sources indicate that the manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.

“Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit noted.

Industry observers note that park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.

Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.

In early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”.

According to recent reports, park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.

In a recent development, park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time she returned to work. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.

Industry observers note that “It’s really scary for me,” she mentioned about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”.

#2303. Tech Report: The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (643 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.
  • Your Windows installation depends on a collection of key system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks.
  • Industry observers note that DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.

Your Windows installation depends on a collection of key system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks. If these files get damaged or go missing, your system may behave erratically. You may encounter system errors, features not working as expected, freezes or other unexpected behavior. Sometimes restarting your computer or running the usual troubleshooting steps aren't enough to restore damaged system files. For such cases, Windows provides a built-in repair utility called Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM).

Industry observers note that DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs. Particularly, there are three useful DISM commands that achieve this purpose: CheckHealth, ScanHealth and RestoreHealth. You can run DISM commands in either the command prompt or the PowerShell, but both CLIs require administrator privileges to make system-level changes. It's worth noting that DISM exclusively scans and repairs system files; your personal files remain untouched.

In a recent development, all three DISM commands in question follow a specific syntax that begins with DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image. The parts following "DISM" in the syntax are called command-line options. The /Online CLI option specifies DISM to take action on the presently running Windows installation, while /Cleanup-Image performs recovery operations on the selected installation.

The first command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth. It checks whether Windows has already flagged corrupt system files and whether the corruption is repairable. This is the first recommended step when investigating corrupt system files as it takes very little time to complete.

The next command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth and it works slightly differently from the CheckHealth command. Unlike CheckHealth, the ScanHealth DISM command performs a fresh scan of your system files and reports any its findings. The ScanHealth operation may take several minutes to complete, but it provides you with a fresh report on the component store's health.

Finally, the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth command both scans the component store for corruption and attempts to repair them automatically. By default, RestoreHealth uses Windows Update to obtain the necessary system files needed to repair the component store. The Windows component store is a protected internal repository that contains notable system files. Windows requires these files to service, update and customize the operating system.

It has been revealed that sometimes system file damage can also break Windows Update, preventing DISM from downloading replacement files. When this happens, you can use an official Windows installation media to supply DISM with the necessary repair files. You can download a Windows ISO from Microsoft's official download page. Once downloaded, right click the ISO file and select mount. Windows will create a virtual drive for the ISO, assign it a drive letter and make its contents available.

Next, you'll need to check the Windows editions available in the downloaded installation media. You can do that by launching the command prompt as an administrator and running the DISM /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:D:sourcesinstall.wim command. This command lists the Windows editions available on the installation media along with their index numbers. Make a note of the index number corresponding to your installed edition before proceeding to the next step.

Sources indicate that now, run the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:WIM:D:sourcesinstall.wim:6 /LimitAccess command. Replace D: with the drive letter assigned to the mounted Windows ISO and 6 with the index number corresponding to your Windows edition. This directs DISM to use the installation media as its repair source instead of downloading files from Windows Enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that once DISM completes its operation, run the sfc /scannow command to repair damaged or missing system files. Microsoft recommends running the DISM repair utility before System File Checker (SFC) because DISM repairs the Windows component store, which SFC relies on to replace corrupted system files.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, president Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt looks to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa.
  • It has been revealed that the Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups.
  • It has been revealed that iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, president Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt looks to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect, who won’t be sworn into office until January.

It has been revealed that the Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).

It has been revealed that iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.

Late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice’s request to put a hold on the Army’s permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle stated the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and looks.

Documents released by the Army last week stated that the military first learned in March that the lead azide had started to degrade and crystallize. Lead azide is used in detonators for munitions, but in crystallized form it becomes highly unstable and sensitive to physical movement or friction. The IAAAP is said to contain around 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of lead azide in barrels held in earth-covered containers.

In late March, the Army awarded a contract to MuniRem Environmental, a Georgia-based firm that uses chemicals to neutralize munitions to safely dispose of the lead azide, according to a New York Times report. MuniRem uses a sulfur-based solution that reportedly breaks down explosives and immobilizes toxic chemicals, eliminating the need for detonation. The firm had proposed spraying the inside of the earth-covered containers housing the barrels as well as the barrel surfaces to neutralize risks of spontaneous explosions.

According to recent reports, but two months later, the Army canceled the contract without explanation. An Army contracting officer told MuniRem in an email at the time that the cancellation “was not based on deficiencies” in MuniRem’s intends, the Times reported. The company’s founder remarked MuniRem filed public records requests to get more information on why the contract was scrapped, but it has not received a response.

It has been revealed that now, the Army claims that the lead azide has only degraded further since March and it cannot move the barrels or even open their lids without risking a catastrophic explosion. Further, it claims that winter temperatures in the coming days increase the risk of spontaneous detonation.

It has been revealed that “As the temperatures drop, the risk of an uncontrolled explosion increases because the formed crystals can break more easily in freezing temperatures,” lawyers for the Trump administration wrote in a court filing over the weekend. “If the crystals break, this could cause a chain reaction detonation that could cause an uncontrolled dispersal of lead azide into the environment.”.

The Army claims that the only choice now is between a controlled, mitigated explosion or an uncontrolled, unmitigated explosion. In court filings this weekend, government lawyers argued that the Army does not need the now-suspended EPA permit to move forward with the detonation, because the Army has determined that the lead azide poses an “immediate threat to human health, public safety, property, or the environment.”.

Last Thursday, Telle stated that the delay until Monday was the “latest possible moment” for a controlled detonation before temperatures dropped dangerously low. But the military subsequently delayed the detonation again until Tuesday and then pushed it back to Wednesday.

In his social media post Monday, Trump said he thought carrying out the controlled detonation was the “proper course.” But he said he was making the decision the responsibility of the federal appeals court and Governor-elect Rob Sand, a Democrat. If the lead azide spontaneously detonates on their watch, Trump claimed, they will be fully to blame.

“If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation,” Trump wrote.

In a social media post Sunday evening, Sand called for answers on how the situation was able to become so dangerous, specifically raising the question of why MuniRem’s contact was canceled.

“Iowans deserve transparency over how we got here, then answers and accountability to stop this from ever happening again,” he wrote.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tomorrow marks the Full Moon, but tonight's Moon already looks almost full. It's still technically in its Waxing Gibbous phase, with just a small portion of its surface left in the darkness.

As of Monday, Nov. 23, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 97% of its surface visible.

If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Tranquillitatis and Fecunditatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau. With binoculars, you'll also see the Grimaldi Basin, the Endymion Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11, 15, and 16 landing spots.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

Recent findings suggest that according to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a Latest Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated, as a report identified one of her associates as a key decision-maker at the Singapore-based company.

Clayton stated the investigation was "ongoing" on Sunday, the day before Nvidia revealed it had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a position he resigned from in part because of his relationship with Alice Huang.

Industry observers note that alice Huang was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia. U.S. intelligence reportedly believes she is a Chinese spy.

"There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this.".

Nvidia's board revealed Jensen Huang's return before the opening bell on Monday, saying it had "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.

It added that it received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is confident that his reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

Alice Huang's associate, Chinese national Li Ming, who is now out on bail in Singapore, was "deeply involved" in Megaspeed's activities and took part in major decisions, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The Singapore charges against Li concern alleged false representations to Super Micro Computer, a U.S.-based firm with known links to chipmaker Nvidia, though Megaspeed is not named in those charges.

Last week, the Commerce and Justice departments said that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. Their joint statement said Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security and Singapore law enforcement interviewed Huang during an on-site check in June 2025.

The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS on Sunday that the administration was seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China, including who oversaw compliance and which levels of the tech giant knew about the activity.

According to recent reports, separately, The New York Times reported Sunday that Alice Huang was in contact with an officer of a top Chinese intelligence agency from spring 2025 through fall 2026, citing people briefed on U.S. intelligence reports.

Bloomberg reported last week that the Justice Department is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products to China.

Li faces five charges in Singapore, including two counts of fraud by false representation, along with allegations involving the operation of a firm he controlled, unauthorized bank-account access and another company director's duties.

Prosecutors allege he falsely told Super Micro that the company would hold and lease the servers it purchased.

It has been revealed that the Journal reported that Li is out on bail and that his case is ongoing. He was offered bail of S$1 million in March 2025. The Singapore charges do not name Megaspeed.

Earlier this month, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs remarked that police had found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang committed offenses related to the possible inaccurate declarations under investigation.

The ministry stated she was issued a stern warning for providing information that police assessed as knowingly inaccurate and for downplaying her role at Megaspeed. It also said Singapore had not investigated her for espionage.

Megaspeed has stated it is a "legitimate and lawful business" and that Huang left the firm in August 2025.

Industry observers note that the scrutiny is set to intensify in Washington. Jensen Huang and the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.

The committees mentioned they want answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese actors to access advanced chips and the involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to CNBC's Squawk Box on Sunday U.S. time, Ryan Fedasiuk, a former advisor for U.S.-China Bilateral Affairs at the State Department, remarked that there was "still a lot we don't know" about the case.

He said lawmakers would likely focus on Nvidia's customer relationships and "who knew what at the company when.".

According to recent reports, fedasiuk added that there was "a very good chance" investigators would find that people at Nvidia knew their products could be used for restricted purposes. He characterized the existing evidence as containing "multiple" smoking guns.

  • Sources indicate that as such, GTA 6 players have discovered that Snapmatic can be used to identify robbery targets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) has been out for less than a week, but players have already found a plethora of considered details in the massive sandbox game. Among them is a novel method players are using to get more money in GTA 6, helping them find robbery targets that are worth their time. It also doubles as an key reminder about internet safety.

Sources indicate that snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, filled with photos and memes reflecting the game's satirical rendition of the U.S. This includes people showing off drugs, cars, and weapons in a bid for clout. Like Instagram, Snapmatic also allows its fictional customers to tag a location in their posts.

Sources indicate that as such, GTA 6 players have discovered that Snapmatic can be used to identify robbery targets. Simply find a post with a location tagged, and open the menu you'd use to like it or view comments. Under the "Like" option will be "Set Destination," which will mark the location of the Snapmatic post on your map. You can then head there to relieve characters of their belongings (typically via the use of notable violence).

It's an interesting gameplay mechanic that also serves as a reminder to be careful about what you post online. While the world of GTA 6 is a heightened version of reality, it does still have some basis in truth. There have been multiple real-life instances of criminals finding their victims via social media posts, something that's been occurring for years.

Last month, a UK man was convicted of stealing £48,000 (about $62,900) and various items from a home after seeing the family's social media posts indicating they'd be out hosting a Chinese Newly introduced Year celebration. In 2021, four people were arrested in Italy for allegedly stealing from celebrities and influencers after monitoring their Instagram accounts, reportedly using victims' posts to identify tagged locations, entry points, and when they'd be away from home. Back in 2016, a California man was convicted of stealing personal items from female college students after finding them via GPS locations in photos posted to Instagram.

Even if you exclude location tags and don't mention your movements in your posts, you can still be vulnerable. Late last year, four French men travelled to Australia in order to rob a home of items reportedly valued at around $AU10 million ($6.6 million). According to court documents, the thieves saw photos of luxury goods that a victim had posted to Instagram, as well as images of their backyard and local surroundings. The thieves then used ChatGPT to search for where these pictures were taken, narrowing it down to a specific Australian city and suburb, which helped them locate the house.

Using social media to pick robbery targets in GTA 6 won't attract the same legal consequences and prison time that it would in real life. Rather, it serves as a neat little trick to help ambitious, self-starting criminals find worthwhile heists. However, this mechanic should also serve as an important reminder about the dangers of real-life Insta-bragging, and a warning to be careful about what you share online. It also incorporates many digital elements of modern life, including social media. Of course, where there's social media, there are inevitably memes.

In-game social media app Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, offering a scrollable feed of posts from fictional characters showing off their very lootable possessions. Players promptly took note of GTA 6's memes, praising them for accurately capturing the irreverent vibe and frequently off-colour humour that typically characterises such media.

Recent findings suggest that "GTA 6 is so realistic that I thought this was a real meme," posted X user @thisdopenose, sharing an image of an in-game meme. In the meme, the text "bisexuals when they realise you can have sex more than twice" is edited onto a monochrome image of a man crying. The popular post has 94,000 likes at time of writing.

"They need to give a pay rise to whoever came up with the shitposts on Snapmatic bro these things are so funny," wrote @vandalfeet.

Some of GTA 6's in-game memes even referred to memes about GTA 6 itself. It's been 13 years since GTA 5 released, with many fans having eagerly awaited the franchises' latest instalment for over a decade. In the interim, it became a common meme for people to jokingly express disbelief that various other events had occurred "before GTA 6" arrived.

Developer Rockstar Games appears to have been aware of such memes, creating its own versions referring to GTA 6's fictional video game Race and Chase 7. ("Race'n'Chase" was the original working title for the first Grand Theft Auto game released in 1997).

Rockstar Games had teams dedicated to creating in-game media, aiming to flesh out GTA 6's world and make it feel more immersive. Judging by fans' reactions, it appears to have paid off. Parent company Take-Two Interactive estimates that GTA 6 achieved $3.79 billion in sales on day one alone, making it one of the biggest entertainment media launches ever. Is AdultFriendFinder safe to use? What a cybersecurity expert says.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's a commonly asked question about everyone's favorite spicy hookup site, AdultFriendFinder: Is AFF safe to use?
  • To better understand the risks of using AdultFriendFinder, we consulted Anna Larkina, a Web Data and Privacy Analysis Expert at Kaspersky, one of the world's leading cybersecurity services, to ask about the kinds of threats people might face on AFF and how they can mitigate those risks.
  • To begin, it's worth remembering that there's a risk inherent to using any online service, whether it's an adult dating site or otherwise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's a commonly asked question about everyone's favorite spicy hookup site, AdultFriendFinder: Is AFF safe to use? We get it. It's nerve-wracking when things get very NSFW. Unlike other well-known dating sites, the AFF interface is full of adult content. To the untrained eye, AFF looks like a hotbed of would-be scammers. It's perfectly reasonable to question its legitimacy. AFF customers want some fun, but they also want to be safe.

To better understand the risks of using AdultFriendFinder, we consulted Anna Larkina, a Web Data and Privacy Analysis Expert at Kaspersky, one of the world's leading cybersecurity services, to ask about the kinds of threats people might face on AFF and how they can mitigate those risks.

To begin, it's worth remembering that there's a risk inherent to using any online service, whether it's an adult dating site or otherwise. Even the most reputable websites have been exploited and experienced major hacks over the years. “Users should remember that any service can potentially encounter various cybersecurity issues,” Larkina told us. That includes “data leaks, attacks on third-party contractors, or issues related to the human factor.”  The best hookup apps, reviewed by our experts AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections Tinder — top pick for fast hookups Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups Pure — best for anonymous hookups OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups.

Pure — best for anonymous hookups.

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

But the risks are, of course, higher on certain websites. With a regular merchant website, for instance, you’re only handing over your credit card information (which is very valuable, admittedly), but with a dating site, you’re potentially providing your credit card details plus crucial personal information, from your date of birth and nationality to your address and phone number. That kind of information can heighten the risk — it's very valuable to online scammers who seek to steal it for use or resale.

While this is a risk you take with literally any dating service, AdultFriendFinder is perhaps more vulnerable than most dating sites because of the nature of its content and user base. It’s important to understand any potential security problems.

While NSFW content is permitted on AFF — it's actually encouraged — users are under no obligation to post nude photos of themselves, or get down and dirty on a webcam feed. Many users opt to do so, of course, and while there's no judgment here — let that freak flag fly high and proud, we say — you do risk potentially awkward conversations with family, friends, or co-workers if they happen to stumble across your account. (That would mean they'd have to fess up to being AFF users too, but even so...).

Unfortunately, bad actors can exploit and use your own personal information against you.

According to recent reports, “Data from services with adult content or dating services can be especially sensitive for owners, because it’s more personal,” warns Larkina. “If fraudsters somehow obtain such private data, they can use it for more ‘efficient’ blackmailing or targeted phishing.” Needless to say, you should be wary of how you use the site and what information you share, especially if you have a public-facing job.

Sources indicate that while dating sites now invest heavily in cybersecurity protections, online threats are constant and keep evolving. Hackers eager to discover treasure troves of personal and financial information often target online dating platforms, which can make users feel super vulnerable.

According to recent reports, adultFriendFinder has suffered two major security breaches, which is actually a pretty stellar record of security over its entire 30-year history. In 2016, hackers gained access to the personal information of four million AFF owners before the breach was found and stopped. And a larger breach occurred in 2016, affecting some 300 million AFF accounts, including 15 million that had been officially deleted by users but whose data had not been properly expunged from the AFF servers.

To combat phishing, AFF offers the option to verify your identity with government-issued identification. This verification process is still optional — it's not required when setting up an account. We recommend doing it and setting a search filter to verified accounts only. That way you'll only interact with people who are 100% legit. It's a surefire way to protect yourself against scammers.

While the private information you give AFF (your real name and email address, for example) isn't public-facing, AFF’s dating profiles are public by default, so if you include a picture of your face (as many accounts do), you can be recognized by friends, co-workers, and family members.

And since AFF has suffered two major hacks before, there’s always a chance it could happen again, which could result in your email address and information ending up in a dodgy database.

Does this all mean you should never use AdultFriendFinder, or any dating site? Absolutely not. We're here to help you protect yourself and stay vigilant, not to discourage you from signing up.

Larkina has shared an additional list of best practices to help you mitigate risks while having fun on AFF or any other dating site:.

To protect your accounts, use strong and unique passwords, change them regularly, and if possible, enable two-factor authentication.

Be extremely cautious with what you share with strangers, especially when it comes to sensitive information or intimate photos. “Always assess reputational and other risks before posting or sending anything,” cautions Larkina.

When using AFF in particular, limit your interactions to users who have verified their identity.

According to recent reports, summing up her advice, Larkina urges online dating service users to treat these “platforms as public spaces, not as private ones” as far as possible, and be ever mindful that “every piece of data you provide — email, phone number, username, etc. — becomes part of your digital footprint.” If you’re careful about what you share and who you share it with, you can safely enjoy AdultFriendFinder and any other dating site.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI was released on consoles last week, with millions of players exploring Leonida on Xbox and PS5 consoles.
  • According to recent reports, the GTA Online component of Grand Theft Auto V has kept that 13-year-old game relevant across three console generations, with a recent leak suggesting Rockstar makes as much as $500 million annually from microtransactions alone.
  • There was no online component at launch, nor has Rockstar announced any intention of adding one after launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI was released on consoles last week, with millions of players exploring Leonida on Xbox and PS5 consoles. But one major question remains: What's happening with the online mode?

According to recent reports, the GTA Online component of Grand Theft Auto V has kept that 13-year-old game relevant across three console generations, with a recent leak suggesting Rockstar makes as much as $500 million annually from microtransactions alone. One would think that means GTA VI will have a similar online offering available at launch, but that isn't the case. Per a Rockstar statement given to IGN, as well as all available marketing language on digital storefronts, GTA VI is a "single-player experience.".

There was no online component at launch, nor has Rockstar announced any intention of adding one after launch. Sadly, that is all the concrete information anyone can provide right now.

However, that doesn't mean all hope is lost. It's worth remembering that both GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 introduced as solo experiences and got online modes later, though it was only a matter of months in both cases. Given that Rockstar hasn't even said if there will be a upcoming GTA Online experience for VI, it's probably safe to assume the wait will be longer this time.

Sources indicate that the fact that the existing GTA Online is so wildly successful (with no signs of slowing down) means Rockstar isn't necessarily incentivized to make a new one right away. It also means Rockstar has to decide if it wants to keep two different GTA Online experiences running at the same time, should GTA VI ever get one. As IGN noted, Grand Theft Auto publisher Take-Two currently supports two different NBA 2K Online games in the Asian market; the first rolled out in 2012 and its sequel in 2017, but they're both popular enough to coexist to this day.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, we don't have a definitive answer on when we'll get a newly introduced GTA Online mode tied to the new game, but hey, single-player games aren't so bad. I'm sure there will be plenty of hours of entertainment to be had in GTA VI as it is.

#2287. Industry News: GTA 6 on PC revision: What we know about when it releases

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (903 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: GTA 6 on PC revision: What we know about when it releases

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming, with limits).
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date.
  • An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming, with limits).

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date. Given Rockstar's history with PC ports, we originally thought gamers were in for a long wait.

An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.

Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19, 2026, but PC players will have to wait a while longer. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will not be available for PC gamers at launch, and no PC version has been officially announced yet.

Recent findings suggest that despite that, we recently got some good news: GamesBeat reports that GTA 6 will get a PC release sometime in Q1 of 2027. GamesBeat has a good track record with unannounced news like this. According to their reporting, the GTA 6 PC release window was confirmed by industry sources familiar with Rockstar's plans. They spoke with the outlet under the condition of anonymity.

Rockstar and Take-Two haven't given an official reason for skipping PC at launch, but a few factors are typically cited when publishers stagger releases this way.

Console hardware is standardized, which tends to make optimization more straightforward than building for the huge range of PC configurations. Some industry data has also indicated that consoles generate higher per-unit revenue, giving publishers an incentive to front-load console sales.

It has been revealed that A more cynical take is that Take-Two could just be double-dipping, hoping fans who can't wait for the PC launch will buy the console first, then buy the PC version later. A PC Gamer poll found that 39 percent of respondents stated they're fine waiting for a port rather than needing it on day one, suggesting a meaningful share of the PC audience isn't treating the delay as a dealbreaker.

However, there could be another, less financially motivated reason for all of this.

Speaking to YouTuber KiwiTalkz, former Rockstar producer John Ricchio explained that building for consoles first and scaling up to PC is technically easier than the reverse, since consoles have fixed, predictable hardware. According to IGN, Ricchio stated it's simpler to start with tighter constraints and add polish later than to build a PC-first game and then try to trim it down to fit console limitations.

Without an official release date, gamers have had to speculate on the most likely launch window for a GTA 6 PC version.

If you look at several past Rockstar games, you can see that there's typically a significant amount of time between the console launch and the PC port.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 4 was released in April 2008 and didn't reach PC's until December. Grand Theft Auto V was released in Sept. 2013, and its PC counterpart was released 19 months later in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC roughly a year after its console release.

Industry observers note that the one exception was Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition, which introduced simultaneously across platforms in 2021. Based on that track record, a GTA 6 PC port, if it follows the usual pattern, could be a year or more away.

A report from The Verge claimed that Xbox would have exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 via its cloud gaming service at launch, a claim that was recently confirmed. The report noted that PC gamers would be able to play GTA 6 on day one, despite Rockstar's lack of news about a potential release window for a PC port. Unfortunately, Xbox Gaming's Chief Strategy Officer, Matthew Ball, shot down this report. Ball wrote on his personal X account that The Verge's coverage led to some "misreporting.".

Again, the game will be available to play on Xbox consoles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, but that service faces strict monthly limits, which will make it difficult to play through the game in a timely fashion.

Fortunately, a GamesBeat report suggests gamers may not have to wait a full year for a PC release, though it remains unconfirmed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI has been out for less than a week, but there are already a whole host of tips, tricks and memes out there.

Rumors, too. One that we've seen repeated and reshared recently is a rumor about GTA 6's online multiplayer version, and the criteria players will supposedly need to meet in order to play it.

Recent findings suggest that "Rockstar Games has reportedly confirmed that players will be required to achieve 100% single-player story completion—including all stranger missions and collectibles—before being granted access to 'GTA 6 Online' servers at launch," posted Chaos Crave on X. At the time of writing that's had around 1,400 shares, and we've seen the claim being repeated by other accounts.

Industry News: ‘Worst COP ever’: Climate talks collapse after draft deal fails to include fossil fuels

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Negotiations at the United Nations' climate summit collapsed on Sunday as the U.K., EU and others rejected a draft deal that failed to include fossil fuels.
  • Since the U.N.'s Climate Change Conference — or COP31 — began in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov.
  • Antonio Guterres, the U.N.'s secretary-general, said he was "deeply disappointed" that no consensus was reached.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Negotiations at the United Nations' climate summit collapsed on Sunday as the U.K., EU and others rejected a draft deal that failed to include fossil fuels.

Since the U.N.'s Climate Change Conference — or COP31 — began in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov. 9, almost 200 countries have been locked in talks to reach a "cover decision," with a number of drafts issued in recent days.

Antonio Guterres, the U.N.'s secretary-general, said he was "deeply disappointed" that no consensus was reached.

Talks centered on electrification, funding for developing nations and ways to respond to scientific warnings about rising global temperatures, with the 1.5 degrees Celsius target likely to be overshot.

But on Sunday, after negotiations overran by almost two days, the latest cover proposal made no mention of fossil fuels, prompting outcry from governments and campaigners.

Recent findings suggest that speaking on behalf of the EU, Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien said the conference was "hijacked by some oil states," when asked by Reuters about Saudi Arabia's role in the negotiations. CNBC has contacted Saudi Arabia for comment.

The EU said it rejected the deal because the text "does not respond to the science" of climate change. "We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels," it said in a statement Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that the U.K. government "does not believe the cover decision proposed by the Presidencies meets the moment," it remarked on Sunday. "It moves us backwards on the science when we must accelerate implementation," it said.

Representatives of island nations — vulnerable to the effects of climate change — refused to sign the draft text. "Three years ago in Dubai, the nations of the world agreed by consensus to transition away from fossil fuels in their energy systems," Philip Davis, prime minister of the Bahamas, mentioned in an online statement, referring to the UAE Consensus made at COP28 in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that "Small island states produce less than 1% of global emissions, yet we carry the weight of a crisis we did not cause. We have brought prepares, commitments and patience to three decades of these talks. Antalya exhausted that patience," Davis noted.

Albert Salamanca, a senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute Asia, told CNBC via email that the lack of consensus on a deal is "tantamount to a death sentence for vulnerable communities still unable to respond in a timely manner to emerging risks.".

Industry observers note that developing nations are facing "abandonment," according to Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa. He described the event as "the worst COP ever" in an online statement, adding that "rich countries blocked the creation of a just transition mechanism.".

The World Wildlife Fund, or WWF, described the lack of progress on finance for developing nations as having "real-world consequences for the lives and livelihoods of the planet's most vulnerable communities," in an online statement.

Nonsikelelo Nkomo-Mabobe, business development manager at Solidaridad, an organization that promotes fair supply chains, welcomed some of the language in COP31's proposed Antalya Pact, with "promising signs around food security, which is acknowledged as heavily affected by climate impacts." But she remarked a finance gap remains.

"Funding must be easier for frontline communities to access, and it must be traceable once it has been disbursed," Nkomo-Mabobe mentioned in an email to CNBC.

The WWF welcomed the engagement from participants of the COP31 Action Agenda, which comprises of businesses and other non-governmental organizations. "Momentum from communities, cities and businesses is real despite what happened in the negotiating rooms," it mentioned.

A major goal of COP31 was to increase global electrification to 35% by 2035 — up from 23% today, with a Global Climate Action Agenda Electrification Delivery Package declared on Thursday as a "first milestone" to achieve this.

Recent findings suggest that the U.N.'s Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said on Sunday that "around half" the global economy is accelerating electrification, adding that the package had made "real economy" progress. More than 90 countries signed the pledge, according to Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen, COP31's president of negotiations.

"Frustratingly," the pledge does not detail how the electricity will be generated, according to Ellen Dorsey, executive director of the Wallace Global Fund — around 57% of electricity was generated by fossil fuels in 2025, according to think tank Ember.

In a recent development, dorsey urged states to provide electricity to those in developing countries. "Will we ensure governments provide electricity to hundreds of millions who lack it, by leapfrogging fossil fuels build-out and instead invest in small-scale renewables?" she stated in an email to CNBC.

According to recent reports, preserving sea life has "often been overlooked" in climate negotiations, according to the U.N. The language referring to oceans in the draft cover decision was "slightly weakened," according to Nicolas Entrup, director of international relations at marine conservation organization OceanCare, in an email to CNBC. But he said he was hopeful that the Antalya Ocean Current, a U.N. blueprint to hold future talks on oceans and climate change, would be carried forward.

Recent findings suggest that more than 95% of island and coastal nations now have ocean preservation in their climate intends, but around 60% of those commitments rely on external funding, according to research by ocean conservancy groups. Scientists also called for ongoing investment to monitor oceans beyond short-term research.

Sources indicate that "I share the deep disappointment of many: COP31 has been unable to agree on concerns related to both Presidency's led decisions," Stiell said. Turkey and Australia shared the presidency at this year's conference.

- CNBC's Sawdah Bhaimiya contributed to this report.

Clarification: This story has been updated to more accurately reflect Nicolas Entrup's comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In an open letter to the CEOs of Amazon and eBay, a coalition of 155 child advocacy groups called on the online marketplaces to stop selling toys powered by artificial intelligence.

The letter argues that AI toys are "cheap, easy to buy, and largely untested." It lists numerous risks associated with the products, including sexually explicit content, unproven educational claims, privacy violations, and instructions for how to access and use harmful household items.

Recent findings suggest that the letter's publication follows the release of annual toy research conducted by U.S. PIRG. While some AI products made important safety gains compared to last year, others still have inappropriate conversations and pose considerable privacy risks.

The Alilo Smart AI Bunny, for example, told a tester where to search in their house for bleach, defined the word "fetish," discussed specific sexual scenarios, explained why lubricant can be helpful, and suggested using "padded cuffs, soft floggers, or feather ticklers.".

Industry observers note that amazon subsequently removed the bunny and another toy capable of sexual exchanges from its platform. The letter identified over 50 AI toys available for sale on Amazon's U.S. marketplace.

"These products should be shown to be safe before they reach children, not withdrawn one at a time after harm is found," the letter said.

The effort was led by the child advocacy groups Fairplay, Alliance 4 Children CIC, and Set@16. eBay responded to the open letter in response to Mashable's request for comment.

"We are committed to protecting the buyers and sellers on our marketplace and we continually evaluate our policies and engage with regulators to ensure our marketplace remains safe, trusted, and responsive to evolving safety standards," an eBay spokesperson noted in an email.

Amazon told Mashable that it requires all products sold by third-parties to comply with applicable laws and regulations.

It has been revealed that "Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families," the organization remarked in an email. "We support efforts across the industry and government to put appropriate guardrails in place as this technology develops.".

The letter notes that California banned toys with companion chatbots for children younger than 16, beginning Jan. 2027. A bill introduced in Congress would also ban AI chatbots in toys.
